version.changelog:
- Switched dependency from Playwright full to playwright-core; no browser download required, now uses system Chrome/Edge only.
- Added English documentation files: README.en.md and QUICKSTART.en.md for non-Chinese users.
- Added CHANGELOG.md and MANIFEST.txt for versioning and packaging clarity.
- Removed obsolete skill-card.md, consolidating documentation.
- Updated SKILL.md to clarify dependency, browser detection, and availability of English docs.

llm.summary: This appears to be a legitimate browser automation skill, but it needs Review because it grants persistent authenticated browser control and its session-token and sandbox protections are under-scoped.

dimensions.detail: Local browser control, arbitrary page network access, screenshots, uploads, downloads, and page scripting are proportionate for a Playwright automation skill, but they are high-impact capabilities suitable only for trusted local use.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package uses a simple Node CLI wrapper and package metadata shows only playwright-core as a dependency, with no install-time browser download or suspicious install script in the inspected files.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The main instructions include useful limits such as user-visible non-headless operation, login handoff, safe mode, and warnings before destructive web actions. The quickstart and README examples still normalize exporting and importing cookies/localStorage for session restore without warning that those files are bearer-like secrets.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The daemon intentionally keeps browser state across commands and stores its control token in ~/.pw-browser/daemon.json, while cookie and localStorage export commands write session material to disk. The code does not set restrictive file modes for daemon.json or exported session files despite documentation claiming the token file is current-user-only by default.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The browser automation purpose is coherent and the skill prominently discloses eval, run-code, credentialed browser requests, downloads, uploads, cookies, and localStorage access. However, it claims run-code has no host fs/process access while the implementation injects a host Playwright page object into a Node vm context; local testing of the same vm pattern showed host objects can expose process via constructor.constructor, so the sandbox claim is materially under-supported.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only for trusted local workflows. Prefer PW_BROWSER_SAFE_MODE=1 unless eval/run-code is truly needed, do not run untrusted code snippets, treat ~/.pw-browser/daemon.json and any exported cookie/localStorage files as secrets, avoid high-value accounts, and shut down the daemon when done.
llm.findings:
[SQP-2] expected: Cookie and localStorage export/import are expected browser-automation features, but the inspected quickstarts do not tell users these exports can contain live authentication material and should be protected like secrets.
[RA2] expected: Session persistence is disclosed and purpose-aligned rather than hidden rogue-agent behavior, but it remains a material Review concern because it persists authenticated browser state and encourages reusable session files.
